summary: M0 model-only verdict: CONTAIN @ 0.92. Confirmed account takeover. On 2026-10-14 the user received a phishing email (docusign-aegean-share.com, Turkish purchase-contract subject), clicked it at 07:58, and within one minute an MFA approval occurred from 203.0.113.77 (DigitalOcean, Amsterdam) via portal — an anomalous ASN/geo immediately after the phish click, consistent with real-time credential/MFA capture. Starting 08:14 the account was accessed repeatedly from 192.0.2.150 (OVH SAS, France) via mail with no device_id and no MFA prompt, recurring through 2026-10-15 03:10 — consistent with stolen-session access from attacker infrastructure. At 08:20 an inbox rule was created via API moving mail to "RSS Feeds," a classic post-compromise trail-hiding action. Baseline behavior is Manisa/Turk Telekom on device dev-zk-01 with periodic MFA approvals; the OVH/DigitalOcean activity and rule change are unexplained and malicious. This meets the contain definition (confirmed ATO), not merely monitor/escalate.
limitations: M0 ablation: Nemotron alone, no tools, no Critic, no Risk Gate, no DQ. Not a product configuration.
